claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast, equiatomic, single-phase FCC FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
The intervention changes the composition to equiatomic FeCoNiAl.
Aging equiatomic FeCoNiAl at 600–700 °C for several hours will induce B2 phase formation in an FCC matrix.
The aging treatment will produce coherent, nanoscale B2 precipitates.
The composition must remain nearly equiatomic and have configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Coherent nanoscale B2 precipitates dispersed in an FCC matrix act as magnetic domain-wall pinning centers.
Coherent B2 precipitates locally increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
B2 precipitate interfaces create energy barriers that hinder magnetic domain-wall motion.
Hindered domain-wall motion requires a larger applied field for magnetization reversal and therefore increases coercivity.
B2 precipitation will largely preserve the high saturation magnetization attributed to the FeCoNi base.
Aged FeCoNiAl will have significantly higher coercivity than soft-ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt baselines.
The coercivity increase will correlate with the volume fraction and spatial distribution of nanoscale B2 precipitates.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt derivatives are soft ferromagnets with low coercive fields.
Coarsening or loss of precipitate coherence under overly aggressive aging can eliminate the coercivity enhancement.
Insufficient B2 precipitation under overly mild aging can eliminate the coercivity enhancement.
The optimal aging temperature, duration, and precipitate volume fraction are not yet determined.
An earlier Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy exhibited a two-phase FCC/B2 microstructure.

contradictions.description: The principal prediction compares aged FeCoNiAl with FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, whereas the proposed experiment and falsification threshold compare aged FeCoNiAl only with as-cast FeCoNiAl. Thus the experiment does not directly test the stated comparative outcome.

The initial state is described as an equiatomic single-phase FCC FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy, but the intervention also changes the composition to FeCoNiAl. It is unclear whether the initial state is ternary FeCoNi, as-cast FeCoNiAl, or another FeCoNi-based derivative.
